federal.25C: Ended: there is no 25C credit for a heat pump placed in service in 2026. Public Law 119-21 (signed July 4, 2025; the reconciliation law commonly called the One Big Beautiful Bill Act), Sec. 70505, amended 26 U.S.C. 25C so the credit does not apply to property placed in service after Dec. 31, 2025 (the IRA had run it through 2032). IRS FS-2025-05 (Aug. 21, 2025), FAQ 1: 'The credit will not be allowed for any property placed in service after December 31, 2025.' The IRS 25C page (last reviewed Apr. 28, 2026) says the credit is allowed for property placed in service 'on or after Jan. 1, 2023, and before December 31, 2025'. While it was available, heat pumps had to meet 'the CEE highest efficiency tier, not including any advanced tier', for up to $2,000 a year. Heat pumps placed in service in 2025 are claimed on 2025 returns. The 25D credit, which covered geothermal heat pumps, also ended for expenditures made after Dec. 31, 2025. Per FS-2025-05 FAQ 7, 'If installation is completed after December 31, 2025, the expenditure will be treated as made after December 31, 2025', even if it was paid in 2025.
federal.HEAR: ENERGY STAR certification is the only federal equipment rule found. There is no federal cold-climate requirement. Statute (IRA Sec. 50122, 42 U.S.C. 18795a): the rebate is capped at 'not more than $8,000 for a heat pump for space heating or cooling', and a qualified electrification project excludes an item that 'is not certified under the Energy Star program ... if applicable'. DOE's Home Energy Rebates fact sheet: '$8,000 for an ENERGY STAR certified electric heat pump for space heating and cooling.' ENERGY STAR's HEAR table answers 'Yes' to 'ENERGY STAR Certification Required?' for a 'Heat Pump for Space Heating/Cooling'. It lists ducted, ducted cold climate, mini-split, mini-split cold climate, single-package and geothermal heat pumps as eligible, and states no cold-climate requirement. DOE's fact sheet and Program Notice 26-2 do not mention ENERGY STAR Cold Climate, NEEP listing, a COP at 5°F or any SEER2/HSPF2 minimum. States can set stricter tiers; for example, Colorado paid up to $8,000 only for cold-climate heat pumps and $3,000 for other heat pumps. INSTALLATION: DOE's retail guide (Sept. 2024) lists 'Heat pumps for space heating and cooling' among products that 'require installation by a contractor on the state's qualified contractor list'. PN 26-2 encourages DIY rebates 'with the exception of HVAC system installations'. 2026 CHANGES: DOE Program Notice 26-2 took effect May 29, 2026. It supersedes the HEEHR items of the Program Requirements & Application Instructions v2.1 (Dec. 16, 2024) and renames the program High-Efficiency Electric Home Rebates (HEEHR). Under it, rebates are allowed 'for upgrading HVAC and appliances only from existing electric equipment to more efficient electric equipment', and new construction is still allowed. Homes may 'retain existing fossil-fuel HVAC systems when installing a heat pump'. Homes must use rebates for insulation and air sealing before heating and cooling upgrades, unless already insulated and sealed to a DOE-approved, state-specified level. The statute's own definition still covers purchases for new construction, purchases that replace a nonelectric appliance, and first-time purchases.

Whole Home all-electric bundle per unit: $10,000 single-family, $8,000 modular, $7,000 ADU, $5,000 low-rise multifamily, $7,000 manufactured housing.
programs.equipmentRule: The Whole Home bundle 'must include electric only space heating and cooling (HVAC), water heating, cooking and clothes drying' ('no natural gas'). The page states no SEER2/HSPF2 requirement.
programs.contractorRule: Not stated. LADWP approval is required before construction or installation begins.
programs.status: pilot; open only to owners rebuilding homes substantially damaged or destroyed by the January 2025 Palisades, Hurst, Kenneth, Archer and Sunset fires; first-come, first-served until funds are exhausted

programs.name: SCE Home Performance Plus heat pump rebates
programs.heatPumpRebate: Ducted central heat pump $667 per ton. Ductless mini-split $1,144.80 per ton when replacing a gas wall furnace and window A/C, or $600 per ton when replacing a gas wall furnace only. Limit one HVAC rebate per home, up to 5 tons.
programs.equipmentRule: 'Must be rated 16 SEER2 or higher.' A ducted heat pump must replace a central A/C rated '13 SEER (12.4 SEER2) or lower' and a natural gas furnace rated '80% AFUE or lower'. programs.name: NYS Clean Heat: Con Edison air-source heat pump incentive
programs.heatPumpRebate: Full replacement (old system removed or disabled): single-family $10,000 weatherized / $7,000 standard, or $11,000 / $8,000 in a Disadvantaged Community (DAC); apartment $5,000 / $3,500, or $5,500 / $4,000 in a DAC. Keeping the old system with integrated controls: single-family $2,500 ($4,500 DAC); apartment $1,000 ($2,000 DAC). Customers who got a partial incentive before can get up to $4,000 more (single-family) or $1,500 (apartment) when they remove or disable the fossil system. All incentives are capped at 70% of project cost (85% in a DAC).
programs.equipmentRule: Con Edison's page states no equipment specification. The NYS Clean Heat Program Manual (Version 3, effective Sept. 1, 2026) requires full-load ccASHP equipment to be 'listed on, or that meet the criteria of, the NEEP Cold Climate Product List'. Air-to-water units must be on the NYS Clean Heat AWHP QPL, with a heating COP of '1.7 or greater' at 5°F and 110°F leaving water. Full load means at least 100% of the building heating load at design conditions, sized per ACCA Manual S (2023) from Manual J (8th ed.) loads; systems over 120% may need review. Partial-to-full projects (Category 4) must supply more than 50% of the load. The integrated-controls option (Category 2a) requires controls on the Clean Heat Integrated Controls QPL. The Weatherized tier requires a properly insulated and air-sealed home.
programs.contractorRule: 'You must work with a Participating Contractor to qualify for incentives', and the home must be 'service adequate'. The rebate is deducted from the invoice. No DIY.
programs.status: open, 'subject to program rules and available funding'; no end date

notes: SCOPE: Space-heating and cooling heat pumps only: ducted and ductless air-source, cold-climate, ground-source and air-to-water. Peoples Gas's gas-fired heat pump is included because our Chicago file lists it. Rebates for heat pump water heaters only are out of scope and were not re-checked: Austin Energy, BGE, Con Edison, SRP, Seattle City Light, PSE, Solana Beach, CenterPoint Houston, Georgia Power, Dominion and Clark PU. All checks were made on 2026-10-19; a 'checked' date means a check was attempted that day, and entries whose status begins 'UNVERIFIED' or 'unverified' could not be confirmed on an official page. WHAT COULD NOT BE VERIFIED, AND WHY: (1) ComEd's pages (heat pump discounts, Whole Home Electric, FAQ) render client-side and returned no text, so the ComEd entries repeat our 2026-10-12 data, labelled. (2) Xcel Energy's current rebate summaries are on a robots-disallowed file host, and co./mn.my.xcelenergy.com load only a placeholder. Xcel MN electric-only amounts are corroborated by CEE's current page; MN equipment criteria come from Xcel's 2024-2026 MN sheet (form 23-12-201); Xcel CO is unverified. (3) CenterPoint Energy pages (Houston HVAC and MN ducted ASHP) returned fetch errors. (4) Denver's city rebate page is robots-disallowed, so no Denver city heat pump rebate was checked. (5) Duke Energy program pages could not be read (our Oct. 12 research found them blocked); only Duke news releases were read. (6) No customer-facing PECO page was read, and PECO's Phase V plan PDF gave no readable amounts or specifications. (7) The DOE Program Requirements & Application Instructions v2.1 PDF was cut off before Section 4 (HEAR), so DOE's own Section 4.2.2 wording on qualified electrification projects, including any cold-climate recommendation, could not be quoted. The federal HEAR rule above rests on the statute, DOE's fact sheet and retail guide, PN 26-2 and ENERGY STAR's HEAR table. (8) The New England Heat Pump Accelerator was not verified. (9) The web-search budget shared by all agents in this run ran out partway through, so no new official pages could be searched for. Later checks used only URLs already in our metro files or returned by earlier fetches.
